name: FVSCHEDULE
description: FVSCHEDULE returns the future value of an investment using a schedule of varying interest rates.
tldr: Calculates the future value of a principal after applying a series of compound interest rates.

parameters.name: schedule
parameters.description: Array of interest rates to apply for each period.

basicExample.description: Future value with varying annual rates
basicExample.explanation: B2:B5 contains the annual interest rates for each period.

advancedExamples.title: Fixed rates entered directly
advancedExamples.description: Future value after three years of varying rates
advancedExamples.explanation: Principal grows at 5%, then 6%, then 4% over three years.

howItWorks: FVSCHEDULE multiplies the principal by (1 + rate1) * (1 + rate2) * ... for each rate in the schedule. This models compound growth with changing rates.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Schedule values must be decimal rates (e.g., 0.05 for 5%).
Schedule values can be negative for losses.

commonErrors.cause: Schedule values are text or non-numeric.
Rates were entered as percentages (e.g., 5) instead of decimals (e.g., 0.05).

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: FVSCHEDULE works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between FV and FVSCHEDULE?
faq.answer: FV uses a constant rate. FVSCHEDULE uses a series of different rates.

faq.question: Can FVSCHEDULE handle payments?
faq.answer: No, it only handles a single principal and a rate schedule.
